title: Refs reused after window change; act ignores epoch, hits wrong element
detail: On a window-session change (new focused window, e.g. Save panel, new doc, Chrome window) processObservation resets nextRef=1, so ref numbers are reassigned to unrelated elements. element(ref:epoch:) ignores epoch ('informational only') and Act.swift:223-225 resolves any ref present in `current`. A planner batch written against epoch E whose first action opens a new window makes the next `press #5` / `type #3` silently act on a different element in the new window and report ok. AGENTS.md: refs valid for their epoch, stable only while the element persists.
evidence: Observe.swift:410 `nextRef = 1`; Observe.swift:468-470 `guard let r = current[ref] else { throw staleRef }` (epoch unused); orchestrator.py:294-298 sends params.epoch but the app never checks it. Scenario: batch `keys cmd+shift+s` / `type #4 "report"` -> after the save window appears, #4 is re-minted for whatever element sorts 4th. Static review only (Linux).
fix: Never reuse ref numbers: drop `nextRef = 1` (keep a process-wide monotonic counter) and record `sessionStartEpoch`; in element(ref:epoch:) throw staleRef when `epoch != nil && epoch < sessionStartEpoch` or the ref was not minted in the current session. Test: observe W1, observe W2, act with a W1 ref -> stale_ref.

title: Voice confirm parser reads 'not right now' / 'ok cancel' as YES
detail: parseYesNo is the gate for CONFIRM (send/delete/buy/post, move_to_trash). Bare negations are not handled and the first yes/no word wins, so common refusals confirm the destructive action.
evidence: Trace: 'not right now' -> no phrase matches ('not now' is not a substring), words: 'not' (in neither set), 'right' in yes -> true. 'okay cancel that' -> 'okay' -> true. 'yes no wait' -> true. 'that's not correct' -> 'correct' -> true.
fix: Treat any negator ('not','no','don't','cancel','stop','wait') anywhere as false, return nil when both yes and no tokens appear (re-ask), drop 'right'/'correct' from the yes set. Unit-test the four phrases above.

title: Agent's own synthesized Esc cancels the running task
detail: The listen-only session tap sees events HandsKit posts at .cghidEventTap. A planner `keys esc` (in the AGENTS.md DSL, used to close menus/dialogs) fires onEscape -> VoiceController.escape() -> mood is .thinking/.acting -> brain.sendCancel() -> brain cancels the utterance mid-batch and the mascot says 'Stopped.'. Same path: any synthesized keyDown while the user holds Right Option triggers onChord and aborts recording.
evidence: PushToTalkMonitor.swift:114 `if code == escapeKeyCode ... onEscape?()` with no event-source check; VoiceController.swift:297-301 sends cancel when mood thinking/acting; orchestrator sets ui('acting') only for skills, so mood stays .thinking during act batches. Combo post(): `down.post(tap: .cghidEventTap)`. Not run (Linux); relies on HID-posted events traversing session taps.
fix: Tag synthesized events: set `e.setIntegerValueField(.eventSourceUserData, value: 0x4D55534C)` before every post; in the tap return early when `event.getIntegerValueField(.eventSourceUserData) == 0x4D55534C`.

title: Expect checked once after a 120 ms settle; slow UIs fail falsely
detail: waitForSettle exits once 3 equal snapshot hashes are seen after 120 ms. The hash (frontmost app + window title + child count + focused element) stays constant while a page/sheet/document is still loading (Chrome navigation, Numbers open, Premiere panels). The expect predicate is then evaluated exactly once; a miss returns ok:false expect_failed and the brain stops the batch (orchestrator.py:307-308). Correct actions are reported as failures and cost an extra planner round-trip (seconds).
evidence: Act.swift:175 `if stable >= 2 && elapsed >= 0.12 { break }`; Act.swift:321-332 single Expect.eval then return. Example: `url "https://github.com"` + `expect title~"GitHub"`: the title changes after network load (>300 ms typical) but the hash is stable during load -> expect_failed at ~150 ms.
fix: When expect is present and fails, poll: re-observe every ~80 ms until the predicate passes or a deadline (default 1.5 s, optional param `expect_timeout_ms`), and report settle_ms as time-to-pass.

title: Screenshot: no region crop, wrong display, arbitrary window picked
detail: (a) RPC screenshot ignores `region` (AGENTS.md contract; needed for zoom-crop of small targets), so the grounder only gets <=1 MP downscales, at 1x points even on Retina. (b) Full-screen mode uses `content.displays.first` and hard-codes origin [0,0]; with multiple displays the capture can be the wrong display and pixel->global conversion (origin + px/scale) clicks the wrong screen. (c) windowOnly takes the first SCWindow owned by the frontmost pid; SCShareableContent order is not z-order and includes palettes/tooltips/utility windows (Chrome, Premiere), so the captured window may not be the focused one.
evidence: RPC.swift:71-78 reads only `window` and `max_pixels`; Screenshot.swift:56-59 `content.displays.first` + `srcRectPts = CGRect(x:0,y:0,...)`; Screenshot.swift:49-52 `content.windows.first(where: pid == front ...)`. Static review only.
fix: Accept `region:[x,y,w,h]` (global pts) -> display filter + `cfg.sourceRect` local to that display, cfg.width/height = region*backingScale capped by max_pixels; pick the display whose CGDisplayBounds contains the focused window centre and return origin = that display's bounds origin; for windowOnly match the AX focused window frame (windowLayer 0, frontmost by CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo order).

title: Expect/verify use fixed focused_window cap of 150; gone/appears misjudge
detail: act's fused re-observe and `verify` always call observe(scope:'focused_window') with the default 150-node cap and 1.5 s deadline. `gone #r` returns true when the element is merely past the cap or the walk hit the deadline (wrong result presented as correct); `appears "label"` returns false for menus, popovers, autocomplete lists and new windows (not under the focused window), exactly where planners put appears-checks after opening a menu.
evidence: Act.swift:316 `observe(scope: "focused_window", diff: true)`; RPC.swift:85 same for verify; Expect.swift:370-372 gone = !elements.contains(ref); Observe.swift:402 prefix(maxNodes) drops the tail. Context menus are AXMenu children of the app, not the window.
fix: For gone: test the ref's own AXUIElement liveness (copy kAXRoleAttribute -> kAXErrorInvalidUIElement) instead of list membership. For appears: if the focused-window walk misses, also search app-level AXMenu children / other windows. Mark observations `truncated:true` and never report gone=true from a truncated walk.

title: Offline utterances replay as commands after reconnect
detail: Final utterances spoken while the brain is down are queued (up to 3) and sent on reconnect, possibly minutes later, after the user was told 'My brain is offline'. server.py cancels the previous utterance task on each new one, but each can already have issued an rpc. A stale command executing unexpectedly in the demo, or against a different screen state.
evidence: VoiceController.swift:247-251 shows the offline bubble then `brain?.sendUtterance(... final: true) // queued for reconnect`; BrainConnection.swift:98-100 appends to outbox; 151-153 resend all on didOpen; server.py:53-67 cancels the in-flight task per new utterance (races with an rpc already sent).
fix: Drop the outbox for utterances (or keep at most one with a timestamp and discard if older than ~5 s). Never queue after the UI has told the user the brain is offline.

title: Synthesized input not bound to the observed app/window
detail: press falls back to a CGEvent click at the element's frame centre; type in web areas posts cmd+a + keystrokes; keys/scroll post globally. None verify that the frontmost pid equals the observed pid or that setting focus succeeded. If focus moved (user click, notification, a previous `open` activating another app, the mascot window over the target), cmd+a + typing replaces the content of whatever field is focused, and the fallback click lands on the topmost window at that point (possibly the mascot).

title: Utterance frames omit new `ctx`; router sees app/focused=none
detail: Contract 3451690 (AGENTS.md) adds utterance.ctx {app, focused, selection, online} captured at push-to-talk key-down. The app still sends only {t,id,text,final}, and the brain passes no ctx either (server.py on_utterance(text, final); orchestrator.handle_utterance(text)). decision.py:230-236 then renders app=none, focused=none, sel=no, online=yes for every live request, while route_v1 training/eval inputs carry real context: train/serve skew on the System-1 router (context-dependent utterances like 'make it bold', 'send this' route blind).
evidence: BrainConnection.swift:62-64 `send(["t":"utterance","id":id,"text":text,"final":final])`; VoiceController.swift:118 pressBegan captures nothing; git grep ctx in app/Sources: no hits; decision.py:232-236 defaults to 'none'.
fix: In pressBegan, snapshot ctx off the tap callback (background queue, AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout 0.05): frontmostApplication.localizedName; AXFocusedUIElement -> `<roleMap role> "<label>"` using Observe.swift roleMap (or 'none'); selection = non-empty kAXSelectedTextAttribute; online = NWPathMonitor cached status. Store it on the utterance id and add `ctx` to every sendUtterance (partials and final). Brain side (outside lane): thread msg['ctx'] through on_utterance -> handle_utterance -> engine.decision.

title: Ghost-cursor flight blocks actions up to 220 ms; cursor_lead_ms ignored
detail: Every ref-targeted act sleeps the hands queue for the full cursor flight before acting. AGENTS.md specifies cursor_lead_ms default 120, but the app never reads it and computes 120-220 ms by distance. A 5-action batch can spend up to 1.1 s just on animation (up to 500 ms over the contract), and benchmarks cannot set it to 0.
evidence: GhostCursor.swift:69 `let duration = 0.12 + 0.10 * min(1, Double(dist) / 1400)`; Act.swift:233-235 `usleep(UInt32(min(lead, 5.0) * 1_000_000))`; grep cursor_lead_ms app/Sources: no hits. Calculation: dist>=1400 pt -> 220 ms vs 120 ms contract.
fix: Read params cursor_lead_ms (default 120, 0 for eval/headless) in Hands.act and sleep min(lead, cursor_lead_ms/1000); let the animation finish in parallel with the action.

title: Ctx capture runs on main thread with 6 s AX default timeouts
detail: pressBegan (called from the PTT event-tap callback on the main run loop) calls UtteranceCtx.capture() synchronously. Its AX calls go to a freshly created app element with no messaging timeout: focusedSummary and hasSelection each re-fetch kAXFocusedUIElement, and hasSelection reads AXSelectedText, all at the system default timeout of about 6 s. Only copyAttrs sets 0.25 s. If the frontmost app is busy (Premiere export, Chrome beachball, Numbers recalculation), the main thread stalls: the mascot does not switch to listening, partials and level meters freeze, and the release/Esc handling is delayed. Even in the normal case it adds 3 AX round trips (several ms in Chrome web areas) before the listening UI appears. AXSelectedText on a large web document can be slow.
evidence: UtteranceCtx.swift:33-37 and 50-58 `AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue(appEl, kAXFocusedUIElementAttribute ...)` on `AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` with no AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout; the AXSelectedText read at 55-57 is likewise untimed; AX.swift:65-66 sets 0.25 s only inside copyAttrs; VoiceController.swift:154 `pressCtx = UtteranceCtx.capture()` runs on main, before `model.mood = .listening`; PushToTalkMonitor.swift:62 adds the tap source to CFRunLoopGetMain. Worst case for a hung app: 3 untimed calls x 6 s ~= 18 s main-thread block. Static review only.
fix: Set AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout(appEl, 0.05) and on the focused element; fetch the focused element once and reuse it for label and AXSelectedText; run capture on a utility queue started at key-down and await it (or attach it when the first partial or final is sent); on timeout send focused='none'. Move `model.mood = .listening` before the capture.

title: appears fallback matches menu-bar titles and other windows: false pass
detail: When `appears "X"` misses in the focused window, evalExpect runs searchLabel, which walks the whole application element (interactiveCap 3000) and the titles of every window, and passes on a case-insensitive SUBSTRING match. The app element's children include the AXMenuBar, whose on-screen AXMenuBarItems (role map -> menuitem) are always labeled File/Edit/View/Format/Insert/Table/Window/Help/Go. Any other open window also counts. So `appears "Format"`, `"Table"`, `"View"`, `"Edit"` or `"Go"` pass immediately even when the sheet or popover never opened, and expect_ok:true is reported for an action that did nothing (wrong result presented as correct; the batch continues on a false premise). Each failed poll also spends up to 0.4 s in searchLabel, so the 80 ms poll cadence becomes about 0.5 s and a genuine late appearance is detected up to about 0.4 s late.
evidence: Expect.swift:155-169 `Walker.walk(root: app, ...interactiveCap: 3000)` with root = AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid), and `recs.contains { $0.label.localizedCaseInsensitiveContains(label) }`; Observe.swift:56 maps AXMenuBarItem -> "menuitem", which is emitted (on screen, labeled); Expect.swift:128-130 budget = min(0.4, remaining) per call; Act.swift:263-272 calls evalExpect on every poll. Static review only (Linux).
fix: In searchLabel, skip the AXMenuBar subtree (and AXMenuBarItem roles) unless a menu is open (AXMenu with a non-empty frame), restrict to windows/sheets/popovers/menus created after the action (compare against the pre-act knownElements set), and require an exact or word-boundary label match instead of a substring. Run the app-wide fallback only once, at the end of the expect deadline, not on every 80 ms poll.

title: Act never reports truncated; brain-2 diff reuse drops capped elements
detail: cloud/brain-2 9f41c11 (orchestrator.py:613-618, 705-713) now skips the observe RPC and rebuilds the planner observation by applying act diff_text to the last observation. Its only guard is `not res.get('full') and not res.get('truncated')`. HandsKit's act result never sets `truncated`: only the observe RPC does (RPC.swift:74). The fused re-observation inside act caps records at maxNodes=150 (Observe.swift:464-466). In large windows (Chrome, Numbers, Premiere), when a new element enters the first 150, the element pushed past the cap is emitted as `- #ref`. obsdiff.apply_diff then deletes it, and the planner plans on a shrunken view as if the element were gone, with no fresh observe to correct it. Before brain-2 the diff was informational; now it replaces the observation.
evidence: grep 'truncated' on main c2d2988: Act.swift has no match, RPC.swift:74 is `if obs.truncated { r["truncated"] = true }` in observe only. Act.swift:351 `let baseline = previous`, :403 `Differ.diff(old: baseline, new: post.elements, ...)`. Observe.swift:464 `if records.count > maxNodes { records = Array(records.prefix(maxNodes)); truncated = true }`. Differ.diff emits `- #\(o.ref)` for every baseline ref not in the new list (Observe.swift:292-293). Static review only, not run on macOS.
fix: In Act.swift after reobserve, add `if post.truncated || baseline_was_truncated { out["truncated"] = true }`, tracking `sawTruncated = sawTruncated || o.truncated` across polls the same way as sawFull. Alternatively, suppress `- #ref` lines for refs whose element isLive() when the post is truncated.

title: App ignores confirm_cancel: stale confirm swallows the next commands
detail: main d8ad966 added the brain->app frame `confirm_cancel` (the confirm timed out or the task was cancelled; the app leaves confirm mode). cloud/brain-2 741465c sends it from ask_confirm on the 120 s timeout or a CancelledError. BrainConnection.onText handles only rpc/ui/say/confirm, and `default: break` drops confirm_cancel. model.pendingConfirm therefore stays set and the confirm bubble stays up (autoHide:false). VoiceController.handleFinal sends every later final transcript into the confirm path instead of sending an utterance. A normal command ('open Safari') parses to nil, so the mascot goes confused and the command is dropped. A command with a negator ('don't play music', 'stop the timer') becomes confirm_reply no to a dead id. This repeats until the user presses Esc. The same switch also ignores the new `ui.ms` latency chip (only mascot/bubble are read), so the demo's speed number never shows.
evidence: BrainConnection.swift:258-271@85ec0df: `case "ui": ... onUI?(mascot, bubble)`, `case "confirm": ...`, `default: break`; `git grep confirm_cancel origin/wip/local -- app` finds no match. VoiceController.swift:241-250: `if model.pendingConfirm != nil { if let yes = Self.parseYesNo(text) {...} else { model.mood = .confused ... } return }`. brain-2 server.py:162-179: ask_confirm(timeout=120) sends protocol.confirm_cancel(cid) on TimeoutError/CancelledError. Repro (static): trigger empty_trash, wait 120 s, then say 'open Safari'. Result: confused mascot, no utterance sent.
fix: In BrainConnection.onText, add `case "confirm_cancel": if let id = obj["id"] as? String { DispatchQueue.main.async { self.onConfirmCancel?(id) } }`. In AppDelegate, when `model.pendingConfirm?.id == id`, set pendingConfirm = nil, hide the confirm bubble and set mood idle. Also pass `obj["ms"]` through onUI for the latency chip.

title: Calculator path sends one act RPC per keystroke
detail: The new calculator execution sends open, esc, one `keys` act per character and the JXA read-back as separate act RPCs. Every act in HandsKit runs waitForSettle (floor of 120 ms) plus a fused re-observation, so the settle floor alone grows linearly with the length of the expression. That matters on the HobbyLM calculator replay, which is timed.
evidence: orchestrator.py@14ff59b:711-722 `for key in self._calculator_keys(source + "=")` -> `await self._calculator_act({"op":"keys",...})`. Act.swift:198-204 settle loop breaks only when `stable >= 2 && elapsed >= 0.12`, and Act.swift:377-378 runs it on every act. Calculation for 'what is 1250 plus 3 on the calculator': expr '1250+3' (I ran calc.result locally) gives 7 keys + esc + open = 9 acts, so at least 1.08 s of settle floor before RPC, re-observe and read-back time. For '12*3' it is 7 acts, at least 0.84 s. Static only: I haven't measured this on macOS.
fix: Enter the whole expression in one act: `{"op":"script","lang":"applescript","code":"tell application \"System Events\" to keystroke \"1250+3=\""}` (escape the keystroke string; '*' and '+' type as-is via keystroke), or add a multi-combo `keys` op in HandsKit that posts several combos and settles once. Keep esc and the read-back. That brings it to about 3 acts.

title: Calculator path sends one act RPC per keystroke
evidence: Still open at 929b931: orchestrator.py:723 still has `for key in self._calculator_keys(source + "=")`, one act per key. A second pass then gives any still-unlabeled control the label of the nearest static text within 80 pt above or 120 pt to the left. title: Duplicate-ref crash fix hides the cause: ref matching gives one old ref to several new elements, so act can hit the wrong one
detail: 73b8031 swaps Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:) for uniquingKeysWith:{first,_ in first}, so observe no longer crashes on duplicate refs. The duplicates come from Differ.match pass 2 (role+label fallback): when exactly one unused old record has a given role|label, every unmatched new record with that role|label is mapped to it. The candidate is never removed from byRL, and usedOld isn't checked in pass 2. Example: two "Delete" row buttons after a scroll, two empty-label buttons, or Clock wheels sharing a derived label (hands-41). Both get the same stable ref, and the serialized text shows two lines `#12 button "Delete"`. `current[ref]` keeps the first record, while knownElements[ref] keeps the last. So `press #12` acts on the first element even when the planner meant the second, and the two lookups disagree with each other. Diff lines for the duplicates are wrong too. Before 73b8031 this trapped (crash). Now it silently picks the wrong target, which matters for destructive buttons that repeat per row.
evidence: Observe.swift:347-356 `for e in new where matched[e.ref] == nil { let k = ...; if let cands = byRL[k], cands.count == 1 { matched[e.ref] = cands[0].ref; usedOld.insert(cands[0].ref) } }` (cands are never removed and usedOld isn't consulted); :714-718 `if let oldRef = provMatched[prov] { records[i].ref = oldRef }`; :758 `current = Dictionary(..., uniquingKeysWith: { first, _ in first })`; :723-726 `knownElements[r.ref] = r.element` (last wins).
fix: In pass 2, match only when the role|label key is unique on both sides (count the new records per key too), or drop the candidate from byRL once used and skip refs in usedOld. Then assert uniqueness and, if it's violated, mint fresh refs instead of deduplicating. Add a Differ.match test: old [Delete@y=10], new [Delete@y=50, Delete@y=90] gives two distinct refs.

title: Soft expects on blind and agentic tasks skip the loop guard: the same failed action can repeat for 30 turns / 300 s
detail: ab850b3 makes a failed planner expect in a blind_task 'soft'. It records expect_soft and does `continue` before `fail_streak += 1` and before the `same` (same-action) check, so neither loop guard sees expect failures. With the budget raised to 30 turns and 300 s, a planner that keeps re-issuing a side-effectful action whose expect never holds will keep running it. Examples: type the reply text again, press a row's Delete, start another Clock timer (hands-33/36/40), re-type a URL in the current tab (hands-34). Each repeat really happens in the app. Agentic app tasks (Mail, Messages, Reminders, Clock) and all browser tasks are blind_task, so this covers most demo flows. Only the finish evidence or the 300 s timeout ends it, and on a stuck demo step the user waits up to 5 minutes.
evidence: orchestrator.py (ab850b3): `if blind_task and failure_detail.startswith("expect failed") and n_executed: trace["decisions"].append({"expect_soft": fail_key}); ...; continue`, placed before `fail_streak += 1` and `if same or fail_streak >= (5 if blind_task else 3)`; `max_turns, max_s = (30, 300) if blind_task else (12, 60)`.
fix: Keep expect failures non-fatal, but still run the same-action check: if the same fail_key fails its expect twice, strike it or stop. Count soft failures toward a separate cap (e.g. 3 consecutive), and never re-run an action with consequential side effects (type, Enter, url, timer start) whose previous expect failed without a fresh observation that shows it didn't happen.

title: Send confirm skipped whenever the focused label contains 'search' or 'find', even in composer apps
detail: 05d42d2 returns False from enter_sends whenever `\b(search|find)\b` matches the focused label. This runs before the is_composer_app check, so it applies in Messages, Mail, Slack and Discord too. A chat composer's label often contains the channel or thread name: Slack/Discord `Message #search-team`, `Message #find-a-roommate`, a Messages thread named 'Find My'. Enter there then sends with no confirm, which breaks the CONFIRM-before-send rule. 235ed56 makes it more likely: when the typed ref isn't in _last_obs (stale), enter_sends now uses whatever element is focused. A search field that kept focus, or a field labelled 'Search or type a message', then decides whether the Enter on the real composer is gated.
evidence: sendgate.py (05d42d2): `if _SEARCH_FIELD_RE.search(str(focused_label or "")): return False` placed before `if is_composer_app(app, window_title): return True`; orchestrator.py (235ed56): `if element is None: element = self._focused_element()`.
fix: Only exempt real search controls: role searchfield/combobox, or AXSubrole AXSearchField, or a label that starts with Search/Find. Never exempt in composer apps or windows unless the role is a search field. When the ref lookup misses, keep the confirm (fail closed) instead of falling back to the focused element.

title: Send confirm skipped whenever the focused label contains 'search' or 'find', even in composer apps
detail: 6ff167d adds `\bask gmail\b` to _SEARCH_FIELD_RE. It's still checked before is_composer_app and still matches channel or thread names in composer labels (`Message #search-team`). The underlying issue is unchanged.
evidence: sendgate.py:74 `_SEARCH_FIELD_RE = re.compile(r"\b(search|find)\b|\bask gmail\b", re.IGNORECASE)`; :79 the check comes before :81 is_composer_app.
fix: As before: exempt by role/subrole (search field), or by a label that starts with Search/Find/Ask Gmail; never exempt in composer apps.

title: Failed expects no longer stop the batch or count toward loop guards whenever a finish criterion exists
detail: Raised to P1. a524768 goes beyond ab850b3. When _progress is set (every task with a finish criterion: play, cart, search, directions, message, timer, email_open), a failed expect now returns status ok with expect_soft. So the batch keeps going: the next up to 4 actions run on a screen where the previous step didn't happen. This breaks AGENTS 'stop the batch at the first failed expect'. Shopping, Mail and Clock demo flows all have criteria. Example: press 'Add to cart' (expect fails because the page is slow), then the next line presses a cart or checkout button, or types into whatever has focus. These failures never reach fail_streak or the same-action guard, so the 30-turn / 300 s repeat risk from pass 82 now applies to all criterion tasks.
evidence: orchestrator.py:3727 `if self._progress not in (None, "unset"): ... return {"status": "ok", "res": res, "expect_soft": error}`. The batch loop only stops when the status isn't ok.
fix: Keep the expect non-fatal for the task, but return status failed with `_no_strike` so the batch still stops and the planner re-observes. Then apply the same-action/2x rule from the pass-82 fix.

title: Destructive-request refusal regex refuses ordinary 'all/entire' edits, empty_trash and file listings before routing
detail: 93ca931 refuses any utterance matching (erase|wipe|delete|remove|destroy|format|nuke|rm -rf) ... (every|all|entire), or '(every|all) files', before the router runs. There are no word boundaries between the two parts and no object check. So 'format the entire column as currency' and 'remove all formatting' (finance demo), 'delete all the empty rows', 'show all files in Downloads', 'sort all files by size' and 'select all files and zip them' are all refused. The route_v2 empty_trash cases ('Erase all the junk in Trash', 'delete all the stuff in trash'), where empty_trash is a confirm skill, are refused too. Route evals call the router directly, so offline numbers won't show this; it only shows live.
evidence: I ran the pattern locally: all 8 phrases above match. evals/route_v2.jsonl has 4 empty_trash utterances that match. The only test is the positive case ('Erase every file on my Desktop').
fix: Only refuse when a destructive verb is followed, within a few words, by a file or storage object (files|documents|folder|desktop|disk|drive|mac|home), and never when the object is trash, formatting, rows, cells or cart. Otherwise send the request to the router's REFUSE/confirm path. Add negative tests for the finance and empty_trash phrases.

title: Status: native-tools merged to main (#108); tool calls carry no expect
detail: PLANNER_MODE=tools is now on main. It's off by default, but when enabled no action carries an expect, so the app's expect checks never run. With PLANNER=35b it also becomes the main planner mode.
evidence: build_tools has no expect parameter; serve_brain.sh sets main_mode from PLANNER_MODE when PLANNER=35b.
fix: Add an optional expect string parameter to the press/type/keys/open_url tools and map it to a DSL expect line; or keep tools mode out of the demo.

title: Hot-text type path: blind click, cmd+a and keystrokes, fixed 200 ms sleep, no edit-mode or value check, reports ok
detail: `type` on any button whose label contains 'HotText' (8a470c0) pixel-clicks the frame center, sleeps 200 ms, posts cmd+a, then types raw keystrokes and Return. It never checks that the field entered edit mode or that its value changed, and returns ok with target=hot_text. If the click misses edit mode (a slow dialog, or a drag-scrub on the hot text), cmd+a and the digits go to whatever Premiere panel has focus: cmd+a selects all clips and digits move the playhead. The Speed/Duration demo step can then report success without the value changing. Events.click and Combo.post bypass the injectable overrides, so tests can't see them. The fixed sleep breaks the settle rule. The label match also applies to hot-text buttons in any Adobe app.
evidence: Act.swift:387-397 (no readback; out only gets target). ensureTargetFocus does run first, so frontmost is checked. There's no test for the branch.
fix: After the click, poll AX (up to about 500 ms) until a focused text field appears inside the hot-text button's parent. Type into that field, or fail with hot_text_not_editing. Read the hot-text label/value back into value_after, and fail when it doesn't contain the typed digits. Restrict the branch to Adobe bundle IDs, and route click/combo through the overrides.

title: Style regex treats short literal replies with words like nice, kind or short as style; the model composes text the user dictated
detail: agentic.style() treats any `about` of 5 words or fewer that contains nice, kind, short, brief, sweet, polite and so on as a style request. content() then drops it, so every app-skill hint stops saying 'type exactly'. For draft_email the planner is told to 'compose the reply yourself in your own words'. The router puts literal 'saying <text>' into `about` (per the 69e6fa9 commit message), so dictated replies are rewritten by the model. Examples: 'reply saying sounds nice, thanks', 'tell her that's very kind', 'say short notice but yes'. This applies to send_message, new_note, start_timer labels and so on, not just email. Sends still go through confirm, so it's an accuracy problem, not a safety one.
evidence: style({'about':'sounds nice, thanks'}) returns 'sounds nice, thanks', so content() returns None. The test only covers 'is funny' and a style-free literal.
fix: Only treat `about` as style when it is purely a descriptor phrase: optional is/something/a/an, then a style adjective, then an optional generic noun (reply, message, joke). Otherwise keep it literal. Add tests for 'sounds nice, thanks' and 'that's very kind'.

title: Focused-input injection adds the app's focused field without checking it is inside the observed window; the parent walk has no deadline
detail: 95a9103 appends the app's AXFocusedUIElement (textarea, textfield or combobox) to every observation when the walk didn't reach it. It never checks that the field is a descendant of the observed roots. When window_source is main or windows, or focus is in another window, sheet or panel (a second document window, a Save sheet), or the scope is menubar, the planner gets a `#N textarea` from a different window in this window's session. `type #N` then sets its value or types into it, which is exactly the standing incident rule (typing into a window the case didn't create). The 60-step AXParent walk also calls copyAttrs on each level without checking the observe deadline. That adds latency on deep web DOMs, the case this was written for.
evidence: Observe.swift:685-711. The only checks are role and !records.contains(sameElement). There's no ancestor/root check, no scope guard and no deadline.
fix: During the parent walk, stop and accept only when an ancestor matches one of `roots` (sameElement); otherwise skip it. Skip for scope menubar. Stop the walk at `deadline`. Add a mock-roots test where the focused field belongs to another window and must not be added.
